records.source: לְדָוִ֗ד מִ֫זְמ֥וֹרלַֽ֭יהוָה הָאָ֣רֶץ וּמְלוֹאָ֑הּ תֵּ֝בֵ֗ל וְיֹ֣שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Of David. A psalm. To YHWH [belongs] the earth and its fullness, [the] world and those who dwell in it.
pieces: Of David. A psalm. The earth is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s, and all that fills it, the world and everyone who lives there.

L.1: Of David. A psalm. To {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [belongs] the earth and its fullness, the world and those who dwell in it.

R.1: By David. A song. The earth belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and so does everything in it. The world and all the people who live in it belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: quoted in 1 Corinthians 10:26
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this line to show that any food sold in the market may be eaten, since everything belongs to the Lord (1 Corinthians 10:26).

decisions.choice: its fullness: everything that fills it
decisions.reason: The word (melo') means what fills something: all that is in the earth.

decisions.choice: By David. A song.
decisions.reason: As in 11:1 and 3:1.

records.heading: The King of glory comes in

records.gloss: For he on [the] seas founded it, and on [the] rivers he established it.
pieces: For it was {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who laid its foundations on the seas and set it firmly on the rivers.

L.2: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} on [the] seas founded it, and on [the] rivers {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set it firm.

R.2: He is the one who built the earth on top of the seas. He made it stand firm above the rivers deep below.

decisions.choice: on the seas, on the rivers: the earth set over the waters
decisions.reason: The earth is pictured as built over the deep waters, which God gathered and set in their place (Genesis 1:9-10; 136:6). The rivers (neharot) are the currents of the deep (93:3). The one who made it owns it (verse 1).

decisions.choice: for he: he himself
decisions.reason: The pronoun is stressed: it was he and no other who founded the earth.

records.gloss: Who will go up on [the] mountain of YHWH, and who will stand in [the] place of his holiness?
pieces: Who has the right to climb the mountain of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? Who may stand in the place of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holiness?

L.3: Who will go up into the mountain of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and who will stand in the place of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holiness?

R.3: Who is allowed to go up the hill where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple is? Who may stand in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy place to worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?

decisions.choice: the mountain of the LORD: Zion, where the temple stood
decisions.reason: Worshipers went up to the hill of Zion in Jerusalem. The question and answer, as in 15:1-5, may have been spoken at the gate as worshipers arrived.

decisions.choice: who will go up: who may go up
decisions.reason: The verbs ask who is fit and allowed to come into God's presence.

decisions.choice: where the LORD's temple is; to worship him
decisions.reason: Readable says what the mountain and the standing are about (m1).

records.source: נְקִ֥י כַפַּ֗יִם וּֽבַר־לֵ֫בָ֥ב אֲשֶׁ֤ר׀לֹא־נָשָׂ֣א לַשָּׁ֣וְא נַפְשִׁ֑י וְלֹ֖א נִשְׁבַּ֣ע לְמִרְמָֽה׃
records.gloss: [The] clean of hands and pure of heart, who has not lifted up to falsehood my soul, and has not sworn to deceit.
pieces: Those whose hands are innocent and whose hearts are pure, who have not called on God's own life to back what is false, and have not sworn an oath to deceive.

L.4: [One] clean of hands and pure of heart, who has not lifted up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul to falsehood, and has not sworn deceitfully.

R.4: It is people who do what is right and whose thoughts are pure. They do not use God's name to make a lie seem true. They do not make promises to trick others.

decisions.choice: clean hands and pure heart: right in deed and in thought
decisions.reason: The hands stand for what a person does, the heart for what they think and want (73:1, 13).

decisions.choice: lifted up my soul: the LORD speaks of himself
alternatives: lifted up his soul to falsehood: set his desire on what is empty (many Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "my soul": the LORD's own self, by which an oath was sworn (Amos 6:8), so that the line forbids taking God in vain in a false oath (Exodus 20:7). Many Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient Greek translation read "his soul", and to lift up one's soul is to long for something (25:1): then the line means someone who has not set his heart on what is empty, such as idols. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: falsehood: what is empty and false
decisions.reason: The word (shav') means emptiness, falsehood; it is used of idols (31:7) and of false oaths.

decisions.choice: God's own life (B); God's name (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose soul is meant (m2) and what lifting it to falsehood means.

decisions.choice: those ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes one person who stands for all who live this way; Balanced and Readable make it plural.

records.source: יִשָּׂ֣א בְ֭רָכָה מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וּ֝צְדָקָ֗ה מֵאֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׁעֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: He will lift up blessing from with YHWH, and righteousness from [the] God of his salvation.
pieces: Such people carry away a blessing from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and justice from the God who saves them.

L.5: {{gender:Such a one|He}} will receive blessing from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and righteousness from the God of {{gender:their|his}} salvation.

R.5: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will bless them. God, who saves them, will treat them as people who are right with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: lift up blessing: receive and carry away a blessing
decisions.reason: The same verb as "lifted up" in verse 4: one who has not lifted his soul to falsehood will lift up a blessing.

decisions.choice: righteousness: vindication, right standing
decisions.reason: Beside blessing, righteousness (tsedaqah) is a gift: God declares and treats such a person as in the right.

decisions.choice: such a one / their, with "he" / "his" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The person of verse 4 stands for anyone who lives this way.

records.source: זֶ֭ה דּ֣וֹר דֹּרְשָׁ֑יו מְבַקְשֵׁ֨י פָנֶ֖יךָ יַעֲקֹ֣ב סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: This [is the] generation of those who seek him, those who seek your face, Jacob. Selah.
pieces: Such are the people who look for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, who seek {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face: this is Jacob. Selah

L.6: This [is the] generation of those who seek {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, who seek {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face, [this is] Jacob. Selah

R.6: These are the kind of people who look to God and long to see {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face. They are the true family of Jacob. Selah

decisions.choice: those who seek him: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text writes this word in a form that may be read as "one who seeks him", and its notes say to read the plural. The meaning is the same. The words follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: your face, Jacob: those who seek God are the true Jacob
alternatives: who seek your face, God of Jacob (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: As the Hebrew stands, the line turns to speak to God ("your face") and names those who seek him "Jacob", the true people of God. The ancient Greek translation has "who seek the face of the God of Jacob".

decisions.choice: generation: a kind of people
decisions.reason: The word (dor) can mean a group of people of the same kind (14:5).

decisions.choice: his face
decisions.reason: Readable keeps speaking about God, rather than turning to address him (m2).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.source: שְׂא֤וּ שְׁעָרִ֨ים׀רָֽאשֵׁיכֶ֗ם וְֽ֭הִנָּשְׂאוּ פִּתְחֵ֣י עוֹלָ֑ם וְ֝יָב֗וֹא מֶ֣לֶךְ הַכָּבֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: Lift up, gates, your heads, and be lifted up, doors of antiquity, that may come in [the] King of glory.
pieces: Gates, raise your heads high! Lift yourselves up, age-old doors, so that the King of glory may enter.

L.7: Lift up, gates, your heads, and be lifted up, ancient doors, that the King of glory may come in!

R.7: Open wide, you city gates! Make way, you very old doors! The glorious King is coming in!

decisions.choice: lift up your heads: rise high to let him in
decisions.reason: The gates are spoken to as if they were people. Their "heads" are the beams above them: they must rise up to make room for a King so great, and lift their heads in joy.

decisions.choice: the King of glory: the LORD entering his city
decisions.reason: The scene may recall the ark being brought up to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6), with the LORD entering as King. "King" here is the LORD.

decisions.choice: doors of antiquity: ancient doors
decisions.reason: The word ('olam) means a time long past, or lasting; the doors are age-old.

decisions.choice: open wide; make way
decisions.reason: Readable says what lifting their heads means (m1).

records.source: מִ֥י זֶה֮ מֶ֤לֶךְ הַכָּ֫ב֥וֹד יְ֭הוָה עִזּ֣וּז וְגִבּ֑וֹר יְ֝הוָ֗ה גִּבּ֥וֹר מִלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Who [is] this King of glory? YHWH strong and mighty, YHWH mighty [in] battle.
pieces: Who is this King of glory? It is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, mighty and strong, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, a warrior strong in battle.

L.8: Who [is] this King of glory? {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} strong and mighty, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} mighty [in] battle.

R.8: Who is this glorious King? It is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who is strong and powerful. It is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who wins every battle.

decisions.choice: question and answer at the gate
decisions.reason: The gatekeepers ask who the King is, and the procession answers.

decisions.choice: mighty in battle: the LORD as warrior
decisions.reason: The LORD fights for his people (Exodus 15:3).

decisions.choice: who wins every battle
decisions.reason: Readable says what "mighty in battle" means for the King who enters in triumph.

records.source: שְׂא֤וּ שְׁעָרִ֨ים׀רָֽאשֵׁיכֶ֗ם וּ֭שְׂאוּ פִּתְחֵ֣י עוֹלָ֑ם וְ֝יָבֹא מֶ֣לֶךְ הַכָּבֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: Lift up, gates, your heads, and lift up, doors of antiquity, that may come in [the] King of glory.
pieces: Gates, raise your heads high! Raise them, age-old doors, so that the King of glory may enter.

L.9: Lift up, gates, your heads, and lift [them] up, ancient doors, that the King of glory may come in!

R.9: Open wide, you city gates! Open up, you very old doors! The glorious King is coming in!

decisions.choice: lift up: the call repeated
decisions.reason: Verse 7 is repeated, now with "lift up" where it had "be lifted up".

decisions.choice: open wide; open up
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

records.source: מִ֤י ה֣וּא זֶה֮ מֶ֤לֶךְ הַכָּ֫ב֥וֹד יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֑וֹת ה֤וּא מֶ֖לֶךְ הַכָּב֣וֹד סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: Who [is] he, this King of glory? YHWH of hosts, he [is] the King of glory. Selah.
pieces: Who then is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, this King of glory? It is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the glorious King. Selah

L.10: Who [is] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, this King of glory? {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] the King of glory. Selah

R.10: Who is this glorious King? It is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, who commands the armies of heaven. He is the glorious King! Selah

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts: commander of the armies of heaven
decisions.reason: The hosts (tseva'ot) are armies, the forces of heaven and of Israel (1 Samuel 17:45). The title answers the question with the name of the King: the warrior of verse 8 commands all the powers there are.

decisions.choice: who is he, this: the question pressed harder
decisions.reason: The question of verse 8 is asked again with more stress.

decisions.choice: the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the older "hosts"; Balanced and Readable say "Armies", the wording settled for this title across the Old Testament, and Readable adds who the armies are (m1).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.
